policy: Only models with exact usable ids confirmed by provider documentation enter the default registry; marketing-only names and previews without usable ids wait.
Research previews with real availability (e.g. gpt-5.3-codex-spark on ChatGPT Pro) may enter with status sota for their niche, noted in the description.
No floating aliases (kimi-latest, *-latest). Pin concrete ids so a provider-side model swap cannot bypass this registry.
Every badge names exactly one model. A new badge holder demotes the old one in the same change.
Any change to models bumps version by exactly 1 and refreshes updatedAt.
Deprecated entries keep their replacedBy id for one release so sweeps know what to rewrite, then get deleted.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.description: Anthropic's Mythos-class frontier model and the strongest non-Codex fallback for planning, code review, and orchestration. Smithers selects it only when Codex is unavailable.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.8
models.description: Anthropic's Opus tier. Still a top-shelf generalist and the always-present fallback behind Fable in the smart, planning, and review pools.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.description: The newest Sonnet: fast, cheap, 1M context. It is the primary non-Codex fallback for implementation and cheap tool calls when Codex is unavailable.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.description: Anthropic's cheapest tier, for high-volume summarization and classification where even Sonnet is overkill.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.description: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 flagship for complex reasoning and coding. Smithers uses Sol for orchestration, planning, reviews, and other judgment-heavy work whenever Codex is available.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
models.description: OpenAI's balanced GPT-5.6 model. Smithers uses Terra for everyday mid-tier work, validation, and tool-heavy tasks whenever Codex is available.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
models.description: OpenAI's fast, affordable GPT-5.6 model for cost-sensitive, high-volume workloads. Smithers makes Luna the default implementation, research, and cheap-work model because it keeps strong agentic coding ability at the lowest GPT-5.6 tier.

models.name: GPT-5.5
models.description: The previous OpenAI flagship. Keep it as a compatibility fallback for Codex accounts that do not yet expose GPT-5.6.

models.name: GPT-5.4
models.description: The previous OpenAI flagship, retained for pinned compatibility. New Smithers workflows use the GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna role split instead.

models.name: GPT-5.4 mini
models.description: OpenAI's prior fast, efficient tier. Retained as the OpenRouter compatibility fallback (openai/gpt-5.4-mini); Codex-native cheap work defaults to GPT-5.6 Luna.

models.name: GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark
models.description: OpenAI's first real-time coding model: 1000+ tokens per second on dedicated Cerebras hardware while staying genuinely capable. Research preview, ChatGPT Pro only. Reach for it when iteration latency matters more than depth.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
models.description: Google's best price-to-performance model and the best non-Codex fallback for UI work: near-Pro intelligence at Flash speed and cost, 1M context, and it beats Gemini 3.1 Pro on coding and agentic benchmarks while running roughly 4x faster. Smithers selects it automatically only when Codex is unavailable.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
models.description: Google's Pro tier (still preview). Superseded for coding and agentic work by Gemini 3.5 Flash; keep it for long-horizon reasoning where Pro depth wins.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite
models.description: Frontier-class performance at a fraction of the cost. The floor of the Gemini lineup for bulk, low-stakes calls.

models.name: Kimi K2.7-Code
models.description: Moonshot's most capable coding model: 256k context, roughly 30% fewer reasoning tokens than K2.6, and strong instruction-following in long contexts. Smithers keeps it as a no-Codex implementation fallback; the -highspeed variant trades a little quality for ~180 tok/s.

models.name: Kimi K2.7-Code High-Speed
models.description: The high-throughput K2.7-Code variant, around 180 tokens per second. The open-weights answer to Codex-Spark for latency-sensitive loops.

models.name: Kimi K2.6
models.description: Moonshot's open-source (modified MIT) trillion-parameter MoE flagship: native multimodal, agent swarms up to 300 sub-agents, up to 13 hours of continuous coding. Ties GPT-5.5 on SWE-Bench Pro at roughly 80% lower cost. The strongest model you can self-host.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.description: Superseded by Claude Sonnet 5.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.7
models.description: Superseded by Claude Sonnet 5.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4 (dated)
models.description: Superseded by Claude Sonnet 5.

models.name: GPT-5.3-Codex
models.description: Deprecated in Codex under ChatGPT auth. Use GPT-5.6 Luna for implementation or select a role-specific GPT-5.6 tier.

models.name: GPT-5.2
models.description: Deprecated in Codex under ChatGPT auth. Use GPT-5.6 Luna for implementation or select a role-specific GPT-5.6 tier.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.description: Two generations old. Use GPT-5.6 Luna for implementation and research, Terra for balanced validation, or Sol for planning and review.

models.name: kimi-latest (floating alias)
models.description: A floating alias that hides model bumps from this registry. Pin kimi-k2.7-code instead.
